title: Hidden Gold Scales
next_chapter_hook: Black Xuanwu's first assassination attempt has quietly begun, with the target set directly on the Observer's private chambers.

text.content:
At the third quarter of the Dragon Hour, morning mist still clung to the Golden Luang Hall.

Chen Ji stood in the shadows beside the hall as an attendant to the Observer, his humble demeanor masking the faint warmth emanating from the fragment at his brow. Through subtle movements adjusting his sleeves, he cast a covert glance, taking in the dozens of spiritual energy currents flowing within the hall. The officials' spiritual energy resembled winding streams, yet Black Xuanwu, positioned below the imperial steps, was enveloped in strands of crimson thread—almost invisible, like parasitic insects clinging to a host's bloodline.

Those were threads of dark destiny.

Chen Ji's eyes narrowed, a cold smile forming in his heart: Indeed, something was amiss.

Those crimson threads did not belong to Black Xuanwu's own spiritual energy. They were foreign, parasitic, concealed. They extended from the void behind Black Xuanwu, piercing through the hall's ceiling, disappearing into a direction Chen Ji could not trace at this moment.

"The scent of the old Heavenly Way..." he whispered in his heart.

Three days ago, during the皇都祭天大典, Black Xuanwu had publicly sworn allegiance to the new dynasty, his posture extremely deferential. At that time, Chen Ji had sensed something unusual in that man's spiritual energy flow, but couldn't discern the full picture. Now, with the power of the Tianji Record Fragment, he had finally captured the hidden undercurrent of betrayal beneath the surface.

He nonchalantly lowered his gaze, firmly committing this discovery to memory.

"Chen Attendant, are you unwell?" A cold, clear voice came from beside him.

Chen Ji glanced sideways to see Su Qingyao dressed in the gray-blue attire of an observer's staff member. Her features were placid as always, yet deep within those phoenix eyes flickered a thread of concern. Using the motion of straightening Chen Ji's collar as cover, she moved half a step closer, murmuring softly: "By the third pillar on the left of the imperial steps, those two senior officials have been exchanging glances."

Chen Ji followed her line of sight and indeed caught the fleeting exchange between the retired Minister of Rites and the Vice Minister of Revenue. It was an extremely covert signal—had Su Qingyao not warned him, he would have nearly overlooked it.

This woman's mind was truly keen as a hair.

dialogue.content:
"Those two... are former dynasty officials." Su Qingyao's voice was pressed extremely low, audible only to Chen Ji. "When Black Xuanwu entered the hall, their fingers trembled simultaneously."
She paused, a cold glint flashing in her eyes. "Like exchanging a secret signal."

text.content:
Chen Ji gave a slight nod, his mind already calculating.

Black Xuanwu, the retired Minister of Rites, the Vice Minister of Revenue... if these three formed a triangular alliance, they would be the core framework of the old forces within court. And those destiny threads extending beyond the hall clearly connected to a more distant node—perhaps a secret altar, perhaps a behind-the-scenes figure not yet revealed.

Above, the Emperor was discussing frontier troop reinforcements with his ministers. Black Xuanwu stepped forward to present his views, his tone earnest, his words filled with loyalty. No one among the civil and military officials suspected, yet only Chen Ji and Su Qingyao witnessed this theatrical performance of hypocrisy.

Suddenly, Chen Ji felt the Jade Slip in his embrace vibrate slightly.

It was Ye Qing's transmission.

dialogue.content:
From the Jade Slip came Ye Qing's deliberately lowered voice: "Within three days, Black Xuanwu has twice secretly entered the underground altar beneath皇都. I used demonic path mist to conceal my presence, following and investigating. I discovered he knelt before the seal at the altar's center for a full two hours."

"Seal?" Chen Ji silently repeated in his heart.

Ye Qing's voice continued: "The patterns inscribed on that seal... bear a three-point resemblance to the Tianji Record Fragment's aura. But they appear more like a forcibly distorted, incomplete form."

text.content:
Chen Ji's fingers stiffened.

The aura of the Tianji Record—this meant what was sealed within that underground altar was most likely something of the same origin as the Tianji Record. Why had the old Heavenly Way forces established such an altar here? Was Black Xuanwu's connection with them related to this seal?

An even more terrifying speculation arose in his mind: If Black Xuanwu's betrayal was not merely a simple power struggle, but a conspiracy touching upon the fundamental level of Heavenly Way...

Then the matter was far more troublesome than anticipated.

He drew a deep breath, returning the Jade Slip to his sleeve. The court session continued above; Black Xuanwu was eloquently expounding on frontier defense strategies, his composure insufferably natural.

After the court dispersed, Chen Ji lingered in the hall under a pretext. Only after all ministers had departed did he slowly walk toward the imperial steps.

The hall was vast and silent, his footsteps echoing. He stopped at the spot where Black Xuanwu had just stood, gazing down at the ground—several wisps of crimson energy lingered there, not yet dissipated, like rotting bloodstains.

The Tianji Record Fragment heated up again; the source of that crimson energy pointed toward... the old Observatory of钦天监, long abandoned, in the northwestern corner of皇都.

"So that's it." Chen Ji murmured to himself, a cold, sharp curve forming at the corner of his lips. "That place is the old Heavenly Way's sacred ground for sacrifice, also the core node of the great formation. Black Xuanwu chose that location as his communication stronghold. He knows how to pick places."

Just then, a yellowed paper slip silently appeared on the table before him.

Chen Ji's eyes tensed, yet he showed no alarm—he recognized the manner of this slip's appearance.

This was Mo Xiansheng's customary method of communication.

He lifted the paper slip, seeing it inscribed in archaic seal script with a few brief words: "If internal turmoil is not eliminated, the grand edifice will topple. The golden-scaled creature is no ordinary being of the pond; once it transforms into a dragon, there will surely be thunderous fury. Tread carefully, tread carefully."

On the back of the slip was another line of smaller characters, the ink slightly fainter, as if added hastily: "Beneath the Observatory's third underground level lies a formation that reverses spiritual fate. Once this formation is complete, all who ally with it shall have their fate devoured."

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji stared at those smaller characters, his pupils contracting sharply.

Devouring fate—this was Black Xuanwu's true scheme. He was not a simple rebel, but intended, through that mysterious formation, to seize all allies' fate for his own use. Those former dynasty officials currently believed they were scheming for merit in a new regime, unaware that from the moment they contacted Black Xuanwu, they had already become lambs awaiting slaughter.

This move was truly venomous beyond measure.

He tucked the paper slip into his sleeve, his mind rapidly calculating countermeasures. On the surface, Black Xuanwu held great power, with old and new forces secretly colluding in court; if he rashly exposed the plot, based on current evidence alone, it would be difficult to convince the Emperor, and might even alert the enemy.

But if left unchecked... within three days, once that reversal-of-fate formation was completed, the consequences would be unthinkable.

choice.prompt: Black Xuanwu's conspiracy has grown clearer, yet how to break the局, it all depends on a single thought. Chen Ji, how do you intend to act?

choices.description: Continue gathering evidence without disturbing the snake, and eliminate the entire nest only after thoroughly mastering Black Xuanwu's crimes.
choices.visible_cost: Time-consuming, but can ensure a complete chain of evidence
choices.visible_reward: Obtain more intelligence about the old Heavenly Way forces
choices.risk_hint: The enemy may complete the formation ahead of schedule

text.content:
Chen Ji tucked the paper slip into his sleeve and turned to exit the hall gate. He decided to暂时按兵不动, continue presenting himself under the废物人设, and secretly conduct deeper investigations into Black Xuanwu's connections with the old Heavenly Way forces.

However, the instant he stepped beyond the threshold, an inexplicable chill rose along his spine. The Tianji Record Fragment abruptly burned hot—a warning of impending danger!

He猛地回头, only to see in the depths behind the Golden Luang Hall, a barely visible shadow was gliding along the hall pillars. That shadow writhed like a serpent, ultimately stopping atop the central dragon pillar, vaguely forming a direction pointing toward... the Observer's residence.

Chen Ji's expression darkened slightly.

It seemed the time window for secret investigation was far shorter than he anticipated. Black Xuanwu's布局 was faster and more ruthless than imagined.

He must reassess the situation and make a more decisive decision.

choices.description: Directly report Black Xuanwu's treasonous acts to the Emperor, even if evidence is insufficient, to disrupt the enemy's formation.
choices.visible_cost: Insufficient evidence may result in detention, identity may be exposed
choices.visible_reward: May gain the Emperor's initial trust, disrupting enemy plans
choices.risk_hint: Without solid evidence, one may certainly be convicted of the serious crime of slander against a senior official

text.content:
Chen Ji drew a deep breath and strode toward the Imperial Study.

To hesitate any longer would be to await death. Rather than waiting for the enemy to complete their preparations, better to strike first. Even if evidence is insufficient, he must plant the seed of suspicion in the Emperor's heart.

However, he had barely walked a hundred paces beyond the hall gate when a figure appeared at the拐角ahead—the retired Minister of Rites, that old official who had been exchanging meaningful glances with Black Xuanwu on the court earlier.

"Chen Attendant," the old official spoke with a机理不阳的 smile, "so hurried, where are you going?"

Chen Ji's footsteps faltered, alarm bells ringing in his heart.

The appearance of this old fox here was no coincidence. He was either here to monitor Chen Ji's movements, or simply Black Xuanwu's envoy to intercept him.

It seemed the timing for public exposure was even less favorable than he had imagined.

choices.description: Proactively contact Black Xuanwu, feign allegiance, actually infiltrate the tiger's den, and await the chance to瓦解his forces from within.
choices.visible_cost: Requires bearing immense psychological pressure, identity may be exposed at any moment
choices.visible_reward: Infiltrate the enemy's core, master the formation's critical points

text.content:
A cold smile curled at the corner of Chen Ji's lips.

The most dangerous path is often the safest. Black Xuanwu believed his布局was flawless, yet he was unaware that all his chess pieces' positions had long been exposed within Chen Ji's calculations.

Rather than passive defense, better to take the initiative. He decided to use his"废物杂役"identity as cover, proactively approach Black Xuanwu, and under the name of pledging allegiance, actually conduct infiltration.

Once deep within enemy territory, mastering the formation's critical points, he could then strike a fatal blow.

With this in mind, he straightened his clothes and walked toward the side hall where Black Xuanwu typically held discussions.

However, the moment he rounded the corridor, he encountered a familiar, icy gaze.

Su Qingyao stood beneath an ancient locust tree, her phoenix eyes filled with complex emotions. She had clearly followed him here, and upon seeing Chen Ji's direction, her expression suddenly froze.

"Where are you going?" Her voice was soft, yet carried an unquestionable interrogation. "That is Black Xuanwu's territory."

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji continued walking without pausing, calmly saying: "Let's go see what our General Black is really up to."

Su Qingyao frowned deeply: "Are you insane? Knowing he has something to hide, you still deliver yourself to his door?"

"Precisely because he has something to hide must I see for myself what devilry he's concealing." Chen Ji turned his head, meeting her gaze. "Su Senior Fellow, if you trust me, wait here to provide backup. If you don't..." He paused, his voice sinking slightly, "then consider that I never came to the Observer's residence today."

text.content:
Su Qingyao's fingernails dug deeply into her palms.

She stared at Chen Ji's departing figure, her heart churning with indescribable emotions. This man was always like this—walking the most dangerous path, yet insisting on wearing an air of tranquility and ease.

What was he hiding? And what was he protecting?

She drew a deep breath, ultimately choosing not to pursue him. She knew that given Chen Ji's temperament, her阻拦 would only complicate matters further.

But she would wait here. Even if waiting until the end of time, she would see him return safely with her own eyes.
